'''''Rhamnus glandulosa''''' is a species of [[plant]] in the family [[Rhamnaceae]].<ref name=PlantList>{{cite web| title=The Plant List: ''Rhamnus''  |date=2013 |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/search?q=Rhamnus |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew }}</ref> It is [[endemic]] to [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]].<ref name="IUCN">{{cite iucn |title=Rhamnus glandulosa |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/30333/83023609 |access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref>

==Description==
''Rhamnus glandulosa'' is a small tree usually {{convert|5|to|8|m|ft}} but can grow up to {{convert|10|m|ft}} tall in a good condition [[Laurisilva]] forest.<ref name="IUCN" />

It has a gray trunk and leathery evergreen leaves sawn, with small glands in the axils of the veins.
The [[flower]]s are yellow-green, arranged in clusters, and the fruit is a globose [[drupe]], purple-black when ripe.{{Citation needed|date=November 2020}}

==Distribution==
It is an [[endemic]] species of [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]], characteristic of the [[Laurisilva|laurel forest]]. It is an uncommon tree in Madeira and on the Canaries (where it's listed as [[Vulnerable species|Vulnerable]]) it is only present on [[Tenerife]], [[La Palma]], [[La Gomera]] and [[Gran Canaria]] and only commonly seen in Tenerife.
On Madeira, it occurs on mid to high altitudes, especially next to rivers, in the Canaries, it is restricted to Laurisilva forests.<ref name="IUCN" />

On Madeira it is threatened by invasive species, changing fire regimes in the forest, and increasing intensity of the fires.<ref name="IUCN" />
